issues.description: extract_arch_from_url can return None and the caller blindly stuffs it into the URL path
issues.detail: If the regex doesn't match, the function returns None and use_koji_url_only happily builds 'latest/None/Packages/...'. That's not an error, that's a silently broken lockfile entry that will 404 at build time. Either raise on no-match or have the caller check and fail loudly. Don't ship code that constructs garbage URLs and pretends it's fine.

issues.description: nevra[0].lower() takes the first character of the filename, not the first letter of the package name
issues.detail: Koji's path layout is /Packages/<first-letter-of-name>/<nevra>. nevra here is the full filename like 'glibc-2.38-1.fc39.x86_64.rpm', so nevra[0] happens to work for lowercase names but breaks the moment you hit a package starting with a digit, uppercase, or anything else, and there's no comment explaining why this works. Parse the name properly or document the contract.

issues.description: race condition with koji tagging is acknowledged in the commit message and then ignored in the code
issues.detail: The commit message admits the crafted URL may not exist yet because coreos-koji-tagger hasn't tagged the build into coreos-pool. There is no retry, no verification, no HEAD check, nothing. 'It's fine for Konflux' is not a design, it's a deferral. At minimum log the constructed URLs so the inevitable failure is debuggable.

issues.description: hardcoded arch list and hardcoded koji base URL with no single source of truth
issues.detail: The arch list ['x86_64','aarch64','ppc64le','s390x'] lives in this function, the koji base URL is a magic string, and 'coreos-pool' appears as a substring check elsewhere in the same file. Pull these into module-level constants so the next person changing arches or pool location doesn't have to grep three places and miss one.

issues.description: regex with word boundaries is overkill for a path component lookup
issues.detail: You're matching one of four fixed strings in a URL. A simple loop checking 'f"/{arch}/" in url' is more obvious, faster, and doesn't require explaining \b semantics in a comment. The current code reads like someone reached for regex out of habit. Smaller is better.

issues.description: the old prioritization logic in query_packages_location is now dead weight
issues.detail: Since every URL is rewritten to coreos-pool form afterward, the 'if coreos-pool in url or not existing_url' preference in query_packages_location no longer matters for the output. Either remove the now-pointless prioritization or document why both layers exist. Two mechanisms doing overlapping jobs is how the next maintainer gets confused.

review.summary: The patch solves a real DNF5 bug with a pragmatic workaround: stop trusting repoquery's URL and synthesize the koji path. The shape is fine, but the execution is sloppy. extract_arch_from_url can return None and the caller builds 'None' into a URL string with no check, and nevra[0] grabs the first character of a filename rather than parsing the package name properly. The commit message also openly waves at a race condition between URL construction and koji tagging without any mitigation in code. NEEDS-WORK: fix the None path, document or fix the first-letter trick, and at minimum log what gets crafted so failures are debuggable.
